params.edition: Annemarie Mol, The Logic of Care: Health and the Problem of Patient Choice, Routledge, 2008 (ISBN 978-0-203-92707-6 ebk). Online PDF of that edition.
params.not_reached: ch.2 from 'Dreams or support' onward, ch.3-6, Notes, Literature. A second full-text page returned HTTP 503; a third mirror timed out.
params.observed: In the reached range the consultation scene has the nurse asking 'What is important to you?' / 'What do you want?' (patient as respondent), and there is no statement that tinkering presupposes a partner who pushes back. In the reached range the 'does not comply' is attributed to technology ('Technologies do not subject themselves to what we wish them to do'). That sentence and the phrase 'logics are not actors, but patterns' sit partly in unreached chapters; the former was read only through a search result quoting the same edition.
params.reached: Prologue, ch.1 'Two logics', ch.2 'Customer or patient?' up to 'Product or process' (~p.1-20). Extracted text stops around p.20.

measured_now: The attribution is not confirmed and not refuted. What was measured is narrower: the phrase does not occur in the ~20 pages that were actually reached, and the book's own vocabulary of non-compliance in that range is technological rather than interpersonal. The chapters where 'letting go' and the limits of activism are argued (ch.2 'Actors who let go', ch.6) were not reached in the primary text.
note: 前の行は書き換えない。後続が同じ版の ch.2 'Actors who let go'（~p.21-28）と ch.6 'Morality in action'（~p.74-79）を開いたら、この判定を上書きできる。英語版とオランダ語版は版元自身が全体に差異があると明記しているので、版を名乗ること。無いことは否定の証明ではない。
